highlights.heading: The 0–9 band scale
highlights.text: IELTS results are reported on a 9-band scale from Band 1 (Non-user) to Band 9 (Expert user). If a candidate does not attempt the test or answers zero questions, they receive Band 0. Each band corresponds to a clearly defined level of English proficiency. Scores are reported in whole bands (e.g. 6.0, 7.0) and half bands (e.g. 6.5, 7.5).
bullets: 9-band scale: A universal proficiency scale aligned to the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR).
Whole and half bands: Candidates can score e.g. 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5 across each skill and overall.
Band 0: Assigned only if a candidate does not attend the test or makes no attempt at any questions.

highlights.heading: Band scale descriptors (summary)
highlights.text: The official IELTS band descriptors provide clear summaries of candidate capability at each score level:
bullets: Band 9 (Expert user): Has fully operational command of the language; appropriate, fluent, accurate with complete understanding.
Band 8 (Very good user): Has operational command with only occasional unsystematic inaccuracies; handles complex detailed argumentation well.

Band 7 (Good user): Has operational command though with occasional inaccuracies, inappropriacies and misunderstandings in some situations; generally handles complex language well and understands detailed reasoning.

Band 6 (Competent user): Has generally effective command despite inaccuracies, inappropriacies and misunderstandings; can use and understand fairly complex language, particularly in familiar situations.
Band 5 (Modest user): Has partial command of the language, coping with overall meaning in most situations, though is likely to make many mistakes; can handle basic communication in own field.
Band 4 (Limited user): Basic competence is limited to familiar situations; frequent problems in understanding and expression; unable to use complex language.
Band 3 (Extremely limited user): Conveys and understands only general meaning in very familiar situations; frequent breakdowns in communication occur.

Band 2 (Intermittent user): No real communication is possible except for the most basic information using isolated words or short formulae in familiar situations; great difficulty understanding spoken and written English.
Band 1 (Non-user): Essentially has no ability to use the language beyond possibly a few isolated words.
Band 0 (Did not attempt): Did not answer the questions or attend the test.

highlights.heading: Four section scores and reporting
highlights.text: Every test taker receives an individual band score for each of the four components: Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking, reported alongside their Overall Band Score on the official Test Report Form (TRF).
bullets: Listening and Reading scores: Converted from a raw mark out of 40 into the 9-band scale.
Writing and Speaking scores: Awarded by trained examiners using official 4-criterion analytical rubrics.
Transparent profile: Universities and visa authorities often stipulate both an overall minimum and sub-score minimums (e.g. 'Overall 7.0 with no band less than 6.5').

highlights.heading: Overall band calculation and rounding rules
highlights.text: The Overall Band Score is calculated by finding the arithmetic average (mean) of the four individual component scores (Listening + Reading + Writing + Speaking divided by 4) and rounding to the nearest whole or half band according to standardized mathematical rounding rules:
bullets: Ends in .25 -> Rounds UP to the next half band (e.g. 6.25 rounds up to 6.5).
Ends in .75 -> Rounds UP to the next whole band (e.g. 6.75 rounds up to 7.0).
Ends in .125 -> Rounds DOWN to the nearest whole band (e.g. 6.125 rounds down to 6.0).
Ends in .375 -> Rounds UP to the half band (e.g. 6.375 rounds up to 6.5).
Ends in .625 -> Rounds DOWN to the half band (e.g. 6.625 rounds down to 6.5).
Ends in .875 -> Rounds UP to the next whole band (e.g. 6.875 rounds up to 7.0).

highlights.heading: Writing assessment criteria
highlights.text: Writing performance is assessed using four criteria, each carrying equal 25% weighting towards each task. Task 2 contributes twice as much as Task 1 toward the overall Writing band score.
bullets: Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2) (25%): Quality of overview, addressing all prompt parts, depth of position.
Coherence and Cohesion (25%): Logical paragraph sequencing, clear progression of arguments, cohesive connectors.
Lexical Resource (25%): Vocabulary breadth, precision, collocation, natural phrasing, spelling accuracy.
Grammatical Range and Accuracy (25%): Variety of complex grammatical forms, control of tenses, punctuation accuracy.

highlights.heading: Speaking assessment criteria
highlights.text: Speaking performance is assessed across the three interview parts using four equally weighted criteria (25% each):
bullets: Fluency and Coherence (25%): Smooth flow of speech, natural rhythm, minimal hesitation, cohesive structure.
Lexical Resource (25%): Range of vocabulary, idiomatic expressions, paraphrasing, precision of word choice.
Grammatical Range and Accuracy (25%): Range of simple and complex sentence structures, grammatical accuracy.
Pronunciation (25%): Intelligibility, word and sentence stress, intonation patterns, individual sound clarity.

highlights.heading: Score validity and institutional acceptance
highlights.text: There is NO pass or fail mark in IELTS. Performance is evaluated strictly on a proficiency scale. Receiving institutions (universities, employers, immigration authorities) independently set the score levels they require.
bullets: No pass/fail: Every candidate receives an accurate proficiency rating reflecting their demonstrated English level.

Two-year validity: Test Report Forms are valid for 2 years from the date of the test. Recognizing organizations generally do not accept scores older than 2 years unless the applicant provides proof of continuous maintenance of English proficiency.
Institutional autonomy: A score accepted by one university department may be insufficient for another faculty.

highlights.heading: Informational reference status
highlights.text: This section is provided purely as an educational guide explaining the official IELTS scoring model, band descriptors, and calculation rules. It does not validate, certify, or grade any learner performance produced by this platform.

highlights.heading: Illustrative raw score to band conversions (Listening and Reading)
highlights.text: In Listening and Reading, each correct answer receives 1 mark (raw score out of 40). Because different test versions have slight differences in passage complexity, raw-to-band conversions are calibrated to maintain consistent standards. The table below displays illustrative average raw scores required for key band thresholds:
bullets: Listening: ~16/40 for Band 5.0; ~23/40 for Band 6.0; ~30/40 for Band 7.0; ~35/40 for Band 8.0.
Academic Reading: ~15/40 for Band 5.0; ~23/40 for Band 6.0; ~30/40 for Band 7.0; ~35/40 for Band 8.0.

General Training Reading: Because General Training texts are more accessible, candidates need more correct answers for the same band: ~15/40 for Band 4.0; ~23/40 for Band 5.0; ~30/40 for Band 6.0; ~34/40 for Band 7.0.
Conversion variation: Exact conversion boundaries vary slightly between test versions to ensure fairness.
